# Chapter 1 Overview

This page will introduce the theme of Chapter 1: reference-dependent preferences.

## Why This Topic

This section will explain why reference dependence is a useful starting point for studying modern behavioral economics.

## Learning Goals

By the end of this chapter, readers should be able to:

- understand the motivation for moving beyond the standard expected-utility model;
- describe the role of reference points in evaluating gains and losses;
- compare different ways reference points can be formed;
- see how probability weighting extends the chapter's discussion of risky choice.

## How the Four Parts Progress

### [1a. The Failure of Expected Utility](notebooks/ch01_1a_expected_utility_failure.ipynb)

This part will set up the limits of the standard expected-utility framework.

### [1b. Building Reference Points](notebooks/ch01_1b_kt_exogenous_reference_points.ipynb)

This part will introduce reference points as a way to organize gains and losses.

### [1c. Endogenizing Reference Points](notebooks/ch01_1c_kr_expectations_news_utility.ipynb)

This part will show how reference points can depend on expectations.

### [1d. Probability Weighting](notebooks/ch01_1d_probability_weighting.ipynb)

This part will add probability weighting to the chapter's treatment of risky choice.
